description: We are AI & Data Analysis engineers from the Digilians Diploma (MCIT & Military Academy). Experts in GenAI, RAG, Python, SQL, and Power BI. We combine elite discipline with cutting-edge tech to build high-impact space solutions. Looking for UI/UX developers and space experts!
summary: We developed Flame in Freefall, an interactive research dashboard that allows fire-safety teams to explore, replay, and verify how fire behaves in microgravity. It directly addresses the challenge by bringing NASA combustion data into one place, but it goes further: the system connects every number to its source, with 1,412 records from 10 NASA investigations, a time-aligned 3D replay of SAFFIRE-III sensors, and four evidence-backed key findings. Its importance lies in being more than a data viewer; it is an evidence reader. With its unique integration of PSI Data Repository tables and NASA technical reports, Flame in Freefall labels each panel as measured, published, modelled, or illustrated. It doesn’t just show what the data says, but how far the evidence can be trusted, making traceable research a fundamental priority.
details:
Flame in Freefall is a web-based interactive research dashboard designed to reveal how fire behaves in microgravity and how far the evidence behind each result can be trusted. Traditionally, NASA combustion data is spread across separate repositories, technical reports, and investigation tables. Our platform uniquely brings it into one reading environment, connecting every number to its source and labelling it as measured, published, modelled, or illustrated.

How it works:

Flame in Freefall ingests NASA combustion data (currently featuring 1,412 records from 10 investigations, including SAFFIRE-III, FLEX, BASS, and SAME) from the PSI Data Repository and NASA technical reports. It aligns SAFFIRE-III sensor curves and camera frames on one clock, with ignition marked at 60 seconds, and calculates each sensor’s detection latency using a baseline mean plus k times the standard deviation, so users can see which sensor registers a fire first.

Key Benefits & Impact:

Helps fire-safety researchers find which sensor detects a fire first.

Aids habitat designers in comparing flame behavior across gravity, oxygen, and airflow conditions.

Supports mission planners in ranking records for Earth, ISS, Moon, or Mars environments.

Offers visual, non-code-based access to large combustion datasets, with CSV export and cited AI answers.

Tools & Technologies:

Next.js and React: front-end web application.

Recharts and Three.js: charts and 3D cabin replay.

Python (pandas, NumPy): for data preprocessing and sensor latency calculations.

OpenCV and scikit-learn: camera brightness analysis and baseline models.

Firewise AI (Llama 3.3 via Groq): answers from retrieved records only, with record citations.
dataRefs: Flame in Freefall: SI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data
